text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating Lucas Wright, an 11-year-old boy whom I am referring for specialized nephrology evaluation. Lucas is a previously healthy 5th grader who lives at home with his parents and takes no daily medications other than a pediatric multivitamin. 

During an evaluation for poor weight gain, routine labs revealed significant kidney dysfunction, though he has not progressed to stage 5 chronic kidney disease. His blood urea nitrogen was raised at 36 mg/dL, alongside an elevated serum creatinine of 1.5 mg/dL. Metabolic workup also revealed hyperuricemia with a serum uric acid of 8.8 mg/dL and an elevated intact parathyroid hormone level of 112 pg/mL. Urinalysis showed persistent hyposthenuria with specific gravity fixed around 1.004, as well as modest proteinuria. 

Renal ultrasonography demonstrated bilateral hyperechogenic kidneys and a small simple cyst in the lower pole of the right kidney; corticomedullary differentiation was entirely preserved. A subsequent core biopsy showed prominent interstitial fibrosis accompanied by tubular atrophy. 

Clinically, he appears well and is completely asymptomatic. He remains strictly normotensive with blood pressures consistently in the 40th percentile, and he has had no attacks of gout or joint effusions. Cardiopulmonary and abdominal examinations are unremarkable, with clear breath sounds, normal heart sounds, and no peripheral edema. His family history is negative for renal problems.

I would be grateful for your expert assessment and recommendations regarding his ongoing management.

Sincerely,
Dr. Clara Jenkins
